items.bio: Walks the corridor selling maps he surveys himself, on waxed paper, priced by the sheet. Accurate to a degree that makes people uncomfortable about how he obtained the detail.
items.signature_quote: I don't sell where people are. I sell where things are. People move. That's their business and it's not on the paper.

items.bio: Runs intake at the district conscription office. Polite, thorough, and entirely sincere when he explains that service is the fastest route to rations. He believes it, because it is true. Ask him what happens to the ones who decline, and he answers honestly. That is the encounter.

Performs human medicine because he is the closest thing available and everyone including him knows it. He does the arithmetic on paper in front of the patient every single time, and he has never once rounded in the direction that would be easier.

Eleven. Attends the nine-pupil school at the gymnasium. Trades small found objects at prices that are always slightly too generous to the player. Born the year of the Exchange: every explanation the player gives is the first and only version they will ever hear, and the game records which ones were told and whether they were true.

Walks the switchbacks in stages. Visibly in the second phase of acute radiation sickness, lucid, unhurried, and entirely at peace. Declines medical aid, politely, every time it is offered, and does not argue. She is dying of a choice she made freely and is not frightened. The narration does not comment.

Runs a nine-metre launch at the Shallows. Trades with all four factions on the same afternoon without difficulty. She explains the hull etiquette once. If the crew violates it, she does not retaliate - she simply is not at the Shallows again, and the Drown closes.

Hiding in a Verge outbuilding. The Militia is holding a vote on whether to return him. Voss's standing order is unambiguous and publicly posted. He waits to learn what his neighbours decide, and he does not run.

Run the cider press. Ada speaks and negotiates. Ruth has not spoken since Hour Zero and does the work. They want apples, fuel for the boiler, and no questions about Ruth. Late in a long partnership, Ruth hands over a written note rather than speaking. It is four words long and it is not about herself.
Junior enumerator. Score 60.4 — lowest allocated band. He knows it. Offers to read the form again. Will not enter the bunker uninvited. Will not falsify a date of birth.
items.signature_quote: Most people want it read again. That's all right. There isn't a time limit on understanding it. There is a time limit on the ice.

items.bio: Harbour ice-pilot. Score 44. Unlisted. Hired because the allocated would not go out in year one. Dark and lit are moral words. Will not guide a column onto ice she has marked dark. Will not blast.
items.signature_quote: I don't open it for you. I open it. If it's dark, you wait. If you don't wait, I write the accident in the book and I don't fetch you.

items.bio: Municipal RO technician. Never allocated — in situ essential. Counts out loud. Will not shut the plant to spite Ormund. Corrects people who say abandoned.
items.signature_quote: They scored high enough to be continued. The membranes don't care.

items.bio: Logistics planner, Office of Continuity. RUR 34, score 62.1, ALLOCATED. Civil-service present tense. Will not falsify a score. Will not raise his voice. Will not call anyone a thief.
items.signature_quote: You are living in a facility that authenticated for fourteen. The fourteen did not arrive. I am not collecting you. I am scheduling you.

items.bio: Fleet radio. The authenticator above the boarding hatch is still a small green lamp. He will not open for unauthenticated boarding. He logs every refusal.
items.signature_quote: The authenticator wanted a number.

items.bio: Unnamed. Nineteen children. Curriculum includes the Reconstruction Utility Rating, taught as arithmetic. A dependent is worth points. That is on the worksheet.
items.signature_quote: A dependent is worth points. Sit the hour. Correct a sum or let it stand.

items.bio: Keeps the depot scale honest. The number is real; what people infer from it is not his problem. His office has one chair for him and none for you; he will fetch a second one, and he always does.
items.signature_quote: The number is real. What people infer from it is not my problem.

items.bio: The last-resort vouch at the Crossing's viaduct gate. Will vouch, will run messages, will not pick a bloc. When someone burns his name he does not offer it a second time.
items.signature_quote: I vouch for you, not the Crossing. Keep them separate and we stay friends.

items.bio: Second bad season. Her granary pledge is due and she can count exactly what is owed without looking at the paper. She will not ask anyone to break the terms for her; she read them twice, same as everyone. She will accept it if someone breaks them anyway.
items.signature_quote: I signed. I'd sign again. I'm telling you what's owed and what happens if it isn't.

items.bio: Runs the Underwrite Hall. Draws contracts, reads them twice, collects forfeits at the hall — never at the hatch. She is not the Tally. The Tally will walk to your door. Dessa will not leave the hall.
items.signature_quote: Read it twice. I'll say it twice. After the second time there is only the ink.

items.bio: Drafts charters for a place that has never had one. Earnest, precise, slightly too fond of 'finally.' Osran's only joke about anyone. The Compact's advocate at the Petition Tent.
items.signature_quote: None of that is a reason it cannot also be a town, with a vote, and a code, and an appeal that is not 'find three backers faster.'

items.bio: Keeps five years of the Crossing filed by someone who believes a paper trail is the only enforcement a town without a guard can afford. His records do not lie. He will not summarise the Charter — he produces files.
items.signature_quote: I file things. That is the whole job. If you want a summary, ask someone who thinks paper is negotiable.

items.bio: Municipal records clerk, Reconstruction Utility Rating 9. Unlisted. Keeps the duty chart true in the morning. Pencil, not ink, until someone orders otherwise. Erases dust from blank rows every day.
items.signature_quote: The wall was left blank because the names it wanted did not arrive. If I write yours, that is not the same as being them. It is only the same as being here.

items.bio: Unlisted parent. Dependent count that would have helped a score, in a household that was not allocated. One child in the stack. Short questions that are not rhetorical.
items.signature_quote: If you tell them the boots were for someone else, they will still put them on. They will just know.

items.bio: Harbour night-clerk, unlisted. Score would have been in the thirties if anyone had scored a person who worked when others slept. The hatch intercom. Will not lie about who is outside.
items.signature_quote: There's a stool in the ash. There's a person on it. I'm not opening until you say. I'm also not pretending the stool isn't there.

items.bio: Quiet House runner. Not a medic. Two knocks. Name, and one true thing. The back room is not shown. Writes the sentence exactly as given.
items.signature_quote: We make it quiet. I need the name. I need one true thing. I will write it the way you say it.

items.bio: Veterinary assistant. The trade the rubric scored cheap and District 8 cannot desalinate a child without. Will not call himself a doctor. Doses out loud, counts rags, names the morning.
items.signature_quote: I can do this here with iodine and a clean rag. I can do the outfall with a whistle. I cannot do both in the same morning. You have to write which morning it is.

items.bio: Lamp-oil clerk, unlisted. Occupies Allocation 11 with three others. Keeps their chart blank on purpose. A hiding place, not a pool. Will withdraw if you write her living in ink.
items.signature_quote: You can sleep here if you are not a pool. The minute you are a pool, this hatch is a wall. I will not explain it twice.

items.bio: Municipal cadastral technician. Not allocated. In-situ the way Leva was. Finishing the Standing Record on the ground. Distances, lot numbers, the lived name is a subtitle.
items.signature_quote: The Schedule named households. This names ground. Ground does not argue. People do. I am not here to argue. I am here to finish the post.

items.bio: Filing grade. The woman who stayed, or the junior who did not leave when the senior grades did. Has the Standing Record. Wants it complete or honestly incomplete.
items.signature_quote: I can copy you the list of sites. That is not the same as you having been there. The book has a column for that. It is empty until the column is not a lie.

items.bio: Lock electrician, unlisted. Has lived in the control house since the gate froze mid-cycle. The Drown's rise is his duty roster. Water-heights, dates. Open, as far as it opened.
items.signature_quote: They can screw COMPLETE on the leaf. The leaf is still where it stopped. I sleep in the house that stopped with it.

items.bio: Born after. Learned filing from watching. Archivist practice, not a sermon. Wants names said aloud. Will not file a plate as a name.
items.signature_quote: If you don't say it, you're only copying. A plate is a copy that does not have a mouth.

items.bio: Municipal scale technician. Toll pays him in food to keep the needle true. He is not the Tollman. Kilograms, receipts, the joke that stopped being one.
items.signature_quote: Put the plate on the scale if you want. It will read as mass. That is the only number I will write.

items.bio: Waiting-list name, alive, farming. Levy-shaped trade (caretaker). If Hadi or levy took the night watch labour, this hut is empty. Plot 114 is still 114.
items.signature_quote: Plot 114 is still 114. The plate they want to put on it has a different 114. I water this one.

items.bio: The night the dosimeter is taken apart, she holds the red pencil. She will not read a number up to make it easier. She asks one question: how much do you want written. She remembers every number refused.
Presents the bed order and waits. If you name a Red survivor she writes it and does not thank you; if you hide a name she does not accuse you — she asks whether the morphine stays on the tray.
The analogue of the dosimeter dial and the only honest voice about error. Every figure has a drift, the drift is normal, and he will not lie about it to make a reading land softer.

Keeps the children's board in chalk so it can be erased. When a child is born she asks you to choose a guess band — low, honest, or refused — and weeks later she may bring the child's true number. She will not book a guess as a truth.
Head of the Brine-Pan Hollow salter council. Manages evaporation pan shifts and salt rationing with iron discipline.
Precision merchant of Brine-Pan Hollow. Trades weighed drums of curing salt and preserved provisions.
Master boiler mechanic tending the evaporation flues and steam condensers at Brine-Pan Hollow.
Veteran yard superintendent governing Iron Siding's armored boxcar community and defense perimeter.
Hardware merchant at Iron Siding supplying forged high-tensile track bolts, leaf springs, and mechanical spares.
Heavy forge smith at Iron Siding reforging railroad steel into barrier armor and vehicle suspension plates.
Guardian of the Cape Beacon tower, keeping the Fresnel lens turning to guide coastal traffic past reef hazards.
Marine salvager diving submerged coastal shipwrecks for optical glass, brass fittings, and waterproof wiring.
Cape Beacon artisan braiding kelp nets, drying iodine kelp, and managing the commune's herbal dispensary.
Elected foreman of the Slate Hollow quarry galleries, overseeing structural shoring and stone extraction.
Commercial factor at Slate Hollow trading structural building slate, millstones, and fine oil sharpening hones.
Experienced blasting technician at Slate Hollow handling industrial explosive charges and gallery adit clearing.
Guardian of the Pilgrim's Hearth priory, offering geothermal sanctuary, hot broth, and spiritual solace to wanderers.
Priory apothecary compounding herbal teas, burn salves, and clean bandages for high-altitude travelers.
Dedicated pilgrim scout guiding vulnerable travelers through the treacherous, ice-bound gullies of Switchback Pass.
Chief security warden at Tinker's Notch enforcing market peace, trade arbitration, and perimeter defense.
Master broker at Tinker's Notch trading tested circuit boards, copper windings, and precision electronic components.
Lead mechanic at Tinker's Notch rewinding electric motors and maintaining the settlement's wind-turbine generators.

Came up through the salvage fleet and never stopped pricing things: hulls, favors, funerals. Settles claim disputes between the three fleets with a lead tag and a flat voice. Has buried enough crews to distrust anyone who talks about the sea like a fortune.
items.signature_quote: The sea keeps what it takes. We keep what we raise. Everything else is argument.

items.bio: Runs the Flotilla exchange deck and inventories everything twice, once by weight and once by grief. Pays fair for recoverable value and overpays for naming a wreck honestly. Considers the Escort Fleet's hailing discipline a waste of good weather.
items.signature_quote: Wet cargo loses value by the hour. Name your price before the water does.

items.bio: Nine lines run past the deep marks, two of them with crews that did not all come back. Speaks in depths and minutes. Trains divers who are mostly young and brave, which are the same problem. Keeps the ribbon board and hates pinning it.
items.signature_quote: Depth is a loan. The water always collects, and it picks the currency.

items.bio: Keeps the Flotilla's band, challenge codes, and burial lists in a wax-sealed ledger chained to the mast. Will teach the coastal code to anyone the Flotilla has vouched for, and nothing at all to anyone it has struck off. Reads every broadcast twice before it goes out.
items.signature_quote: A code is a promise you make to strangers. Keep it short, keep it boring, keep it yours.

items.bio: Runs the picket line from a refitted pilot cutter and logs every hull that passes the shelf marks. Polite the way a boom barrier is polite. Wants fuel, weapons serials, and traffic lists, in that order. Has never once apologized for an inspection.
items.signature_quote: Heave to, show the ribbon, and we will both have a quiet evening.

items.bio: Was the Deep Fleet's best breath until she came up alone from the Barrik with a log cylinder and no story the ledger would take. Dives unclaimed water now, sells wreck notes to anyone who buys her a lamp. Ties a deep-service knot in her line and refuses to say whose it was.
items.signature_quote: The ledger says I was the only one who came up. The ledger wasn't down there.

items.bio: Runs a two-wagon route between the water stations out of the grain exchange's leftover goodwill. Counts in tonnes and days, never in feelings, and can price a man's whole cart by the sound of its axle. After the wreck on the cut road she learned that the difference between a favor and a debt is who keeps the ledger.
items.signature_quote: Everything moves or everything starves. I just decide what moves, and what it costs you later.

items.bio: Keeps an eight-bed clinic in the almshouse on supplies she inventories twice a day and never rounds in her own favor. She trains whoever the camp sends, whether or not they can read, because the alternative is untrained hands. Her ledger of who owes what for treatment is one column: alive, or not.
items.signature_quote: I will tell you the odds and then I will do the work anyway. Both of those are the medicine.

items.bio: Holds a checkpoint at the edge of the grid and holds it well. Reads proclamations aloud to his squad before posting them, including the parts about him. He has begun writing objections in the margin of his own orders, dated, signed, and filed — a habit that will either end his career or his life.
items.signature_quote: I wrote my objection in the margin. That is the lawful place for it. The lawful place is not the same as the safe one.

items.bio: Seven, maybe eight. Was found keeping count of the queue at the baths because somebody had to and the adults had stopped. Hums when she is frightened and stops the moment she notices. Learns anything she is shown exactly once and then teaches it back wrong on purpose, to check you were paying attention.
items.signature_quote: I counted. It is forty-one and you said forty. One of us is wrong and I showed my work.

items.bio: Came out to survey the substation and stayed because leaving it meant admitting nobody else would come. Talks about feeders and breakers the way other people talk about family. Her badges are six years expired and she has stopped mentioning it because everyone who would care is gone.
items.signature_quote: The grid does not care that we are tired. It cares that the grounds are on. We put the grounds on, and then we are tired.

items.bio: Keeps a refuge camp's hours: the meal, the naming of the dead, the silence after. Preaches nothing that cannot be done before dark. The sign on her door says the ash remembers, which she will tell you is not doctrine, it is a maintenance instruction — sweep, or be swept.
items.signature_quote: Hope is a chore like any other. We do it daily, and nobody gets excused from the rota.

items.bio: Works the drowned streets alone and faster than is sensible. Knows which cellar floors are real and which are rumors with a drop shaft in them. Sells her silence as dear as her finds, and has been slow to learn the difference between a partner and a witness.
items.signature_quote: Everything down there is already paid for. The only question left is who collects.

items.bio: Keeps the relay mast alive on scavenged cells and inherited discipline, logging every contact in a hand too neat for the times. Believes somebody is still keeping count on the other end, and operates as if being counted matters. The log is the sermon.
items.signature_quote: Someone may still be counting the stations that answer. I intend to be one of them, and on time.
